subject: ventures/ai-bookkeeper
professional: a CPA who closes the books of sole proprietors and small businesses from bank and card statements and prepares their Schedule C, Form 941/940 and depreciation (Pub. 946). They would check first: that income and expenses tie to the statements to the cent, that a card payment and an owner draw are not expenses, that the balance sheet balances and the bank reconciles to the statement, then that the payroll and depreciation worksheets match IRS tables.

evidence.correctness: Ran the CLI on a hand-built month (scratch dir, node cli.mjs --books books.json import chk.csv --account 1000; import card.csv --account 2000 --invert; accept 0.6; confirm; report; checks; export qbo) and recomputed by hand: income 1,000.00 + 2,500.50 = 3,500.50; expenses 59.99 + 45.10 + 120.25 + 412.00 = 637.34; profit 2,863.16; checking 5,000.00 opening (derived from the running balance) + 1,000 - 59.99 - 45.10 - 300 - 500 + 2,500.50 - 120.25 = 7,475.16; card liability 412 - 300 = 112.00; the 300.00 card payment was paired as one transfer, not an expense, the 500.00 draw sits in equity, assets = liabilities + equity, and the close check agreed with the statement balance 7,475.16. All match. Independent recomputations against sources the author did not write: (1) Schedule SE (taxforms.mjs selfEmployment, year 2025) on 100,000 profit: hand 92,350 net earnings, 11,451.40 social security (12.4%), 2,678.15 medicare, 14,129.55 total; tool identical; on 200,000 the social security stops at the 176,100 base (21,836.40) and total 27,192.70, tool identical. (2) 2025 bracket tax (estimatedtax.mjs bracketTax): single, taxable 100,000 hand from the rate schedule 1,192.50 + 4,386.00 + 11,335.50 = 16,914.00, tool 16,914; MFJ 150,000 = 22,828 and HOH 80,000 = 10,775 hand-checked to the same. (3) IRS Pub. 946 (Rev. 13 Mar 2026, downloaded from irs.gov, pdftotext, parsed by a scratch script cmp.mjs) Tables A-1 to A-5 against MACRS_HALF_YEAR and MACRS_MID_QUARTER: Table A-1 (all six classes) matches to the printed digit; Tables A-2 to A-5 match exactly for 3-, 5- and 7-year property, but 96 cells in the 10-, 15- and 20-year columns differ from the printed value (by 0.01 to 0.05 points, e.g. A-5 10-year year 11 is 5.74 printed, 5.75 in the tool; A-3 15-year year 16 is 2.21 printed, 2.26 in the tool; the 20-year columns are held to two decimals where the IRS prints three). The code comment already says the generated tables can be a hair off; the effect is under about 50 dollars on a 100,000 asset. (4) Form 941/940 (payroll.mjs): one employee paid 60,000 in each of Jan, Feb and Mar 2025; hand: social security 176,100 x 12.4% = 21,836.40, medicare 180,000 x 2.9% = 5,220.00, federal withheld 30,000, total 57,056.40, FUTA 7,000 x 0.6% = 42.00; form941 gave 2,183,640 + 522,000 + 3,000,000 cents = 5,705,640 and socialSecurityWages 17,610,000 (the 2025 base), form940 gave futa 4,200 cents on 700,000 wages. Match. (5) Loan payments (loans.mjs levelPayment): 200,000 at 6.5% for 30 years 1,264.14, 300,000 at 4% 1,432.25, 100,000 at 6% 599.55, the standard published amortisation figures; tool identical. Not 4: no real bank export was used (the repository's own history says 'no real export tried' for nearly every reader), and categorisation accuracy was measured on the author's synthetic year only. The 2027 social security wage base (192,300, payroll.mjs:30) and the 2026 one could not be re-read today (ssa.gov returned 403 through the proxy), so they are unchecked.
evidence.completeness: Walked end to end and worked: CSV import with running-balance check, categorisation with confidence and reason, accept/confirm, transfer pairing, trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, indirect cash flow that ties to bank accounts, ratios, close checks, QuickBooks Online journal export (rows checked), payroll register to books plus Form 941 and 940 worksheets, MACRS tables, loan schedule, Schedule SE. The README's benchmark (node eval/benchmark.mjs --seeds 3) ran: months 4-12 59.6% posted alone, 0.1% of those wrong, 86.2% suggestions right, as the page says. Not exercised beyond the suite passing: the browser page and its ~30 cards (the page test and other tests passed), OFX/QIF/MT940/BAI2/N43/CFONB/CAMT readers, AI layer (needs a model or key), foreign currency, inventory, rental, 1099-K, S-corp comparison. Gaps: cash basis only with optional invoices and bills; no bank feed; VENTURE.yaml still says stage: prototype; the CLI first run leaves every line in review until the user accepts (by design, reports then show zeros and say so); sales tax filings and foreign-currency invoices are stated as not done.
evidence.verification: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/ai-bookkeeper (271 test files, Node 22.23.4): 2371 tests, 2371 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, 57 s. Seeded one bug: ledger.mjs:95 in balances(), the period end filter `(to && e.date > to)` changed to `>=` (the last day of a period dropped from every report). Full suite then gave 12 failures: the ledger property test on 500 random books, the cash flow and cashFlowByMonth tests, the guide's worked example, the statement-balance reconciliation test, and the year-end close tests (reports balance after close, a loss closes with a debit to retained earnings, fiscal-year report). Caught, and by several independent tests. Reverted with `git checkout -- ledger.mjs`; git status on the venture is clean. Limits: most fixtures are hand-written by the same author, so they check the author's belief about a bank layout; 31 files named probe5..probe30 and gaps4/gaps5 are regression pins, not specifications; no test compares a report against a figure from another accounting package.
evidence.craft: Read ledger.mjs (balances, trialBalance, profitAndLoss, balanceSheet, cashFlow), engine.mjs pairTransfers and confirm, taxforms.mjs selfEmployment and estimatedDueDates, taxdepr.mjs assetTaxYear and the table generator, payroll.mjs form941, loans.mjs levelPayment and loanSchedule. Good: integer cents throughout, validateEntry rejects unbalanced or non-integer entries, cumulative rounding so depreciation years add to basis exactly, payroll rows whose net pay does not equal gross less deductions are refused with the arithmetic (checked: 'net pay 40000.00 is not gross 60000.00 less deductions 14590.00; row left out'), warnings instead of silent fallbacks (an unknown wage-base year warns). Defects: README.md is a 985-line monolith mixing a changelog, a how-it-works table and per-feature essays, which a maintainer cannot navigate; ventures/ai-bookkeeper/ledger-1.0.1-py3-none-any.whl is a binary build artifact checked into the venture directory; balanceSheet 'Current earnings' (ledger.mjs:141-157) is all-time profit not closed to retained earnings, not the current year's, so a multi-year book shows cumulative profit under that label until a year-end close is run; pairTransfers (engine.mjs:244) is an all-pairs scan of ins x outs, quadratic in a large statement; SS wage bases for 2027 are typed constants with no source (payroll.mjs:30). Acceptable for a senior JS reviewer with those notes.
evidence.claims: Backed (checked and reproduced): README 'turn a month of statements into balanced books in minutes' (did it with the CLI); transfers paired not expensed (yes, 2 lines paired); 'balance sheet balances' and cash flow ties (printed by report); memory confidence 'n / (seen + 0.5)' gives 0.86 for 3 (categorize.mjs:665-666); 'from the fourth month on 60% post alone, 1 of 1,300 wrong' (benchmark: 59.6% and 0.1% wrong on synthetic data, and the page labels it synthetic); `node --test ventures/ai-bookkeeper/*.test.mjs` works; disclaimer ('not legal, tax, or financial advice') at index.html:454 and per-worksheet warnings; hand-written-fixture limits are stated for nearly every feature. Not backed: README.md:15-18 says boring payees post themselves 'from the second month on', but the benchmark shows 0.0% in month 1, 7.2% in month 2 and 42.8% in month 4, and the README's own rule needs three unanimous choices; llms.txt:5 (the file AI agents are told to trust) says the product 'does not do payroll', which contradicts payroll.mjs, the README payroll row and llms.txt:56; the page FAQ (index.html:448) says it 'does not know ... depreciation, payroll filings', while the page has a depreciation register and the tool has payroll worksheets; llms.txt links the tool at duncan-haywood.github.io, the old Pages address the repository says now redirects; VENTURE.yaml stage 'prototype' against a flagship ledger. No fabricated number was found, but the product's own agent-facing summary contradicts its features.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a freelancer closing a month: import checking and card CSVs, accept suggestions, file the unknown line (Delta, 6180 Travel), pair the card payment, read profit and loss and balance sheet, run the checks, export QBO journal. It finished with correct numbers in a handful of commands. First-hour gaps a bookkeeper hits: a first run leaves everything in review and the reports show zero until lines are accepted; every card file needs the right --invert choice (I first used a contradictory fixture and the payment failed to pair, which the tool surfaced as a review line, not a wrong entry); cash basis only, so accrual adjustments and sales tax filings are out; no bank feed; and no reader has been shown to work on a real bank export, only on hand-written layouts, probe files and third-party samples, so the first real Chase or Amex file may need fixing. Usable as a first pass that an accountant reviews, not as a book of record.
evidence.domain: Compared with cash-basis small-business bookkeeping and CPA practice and IRS sources: double-entry in cents, transfers between own accounts not income or expense, owner draws to equity, bank reconciliation to the statement balance, close checks, journals import to QuickBooks and Xero, Schedule SE (92.35%, 12.4% to the base, 2.9%, half deduction), 2025 rate schedules, Form 941 line logic (wages over the base excluded from social security), FUTA 0.6% on 7,000, MACRS tables (Pub. 946 A-1 exact), mid-quarter test and 179 limits stated as checked against secondary sources only. Departs or limits: 'Current earnings' on the balance sheet is cumulative not current year until the year-end close; QBI deduction is a simplified 20% (it warns); sales tax filings, accrual basis, and payroll filing beyond worksheets are not modelled; MACRS tables for 10-, 15- and 20-year property are generated and differ from the printed cells by up to 0.05 points; the 2027 wage base is unsourced. A CPA would sign the bookkeeping output with a review step and the stated limits.

defects.what: llms.txt, the summary AI agents are told to trust, says the product 'does not do payroll', while payroll.mjs ships a pay-run register, Form 941 and Form 940 worksheets (checked against hand arithmetic: they are right) and llms.txt:56 itself documents them; the page FAQ likewise says it does not know 'depreciation, payroll filings' although it has a depreciation register and a payroll CLI. An agent recommending the tool is told the opposite of what it does.

The headline claim says boring payees post themselves 'from the second month on'; the author's own benchmark shows 0.0% in month 1, 7.2% in month 2 and about 43% in month 4 (59.6% over months 4-12), because memory needs three unanimous choices before the fourth line posts.

No bank or card reader has been shown to work on a real export: the history repeatedly says 'no real export tried', and categorisation accuracy is measured on the author's own synthetic year, so first-hour failure on a real file is the main unmeasured risk.

Generated MACRS mid-quarter tables for 10-, 15- and 20-year property differ from Pub. 946 Tables A-2 to A-5 in 96 cells by 0.01 to 0.05 percentage points (20-year columns held to two decimals, the IRS prints three; for example A-3 15-year year 16 is 2.21 printed, 2.26 here). Under about 50 dollars on a 100,000 asset, but a preparer comparing to the publication will see it. Half-year Table A-1 and the 3-, 5- and 7-year mid-quarter columns match exactly.

Balance sheet 'Current earnings' is the all-time profit not yet closed to retained earnings, not the current year's, so a multi-year book shows cumulative profit under that label until a year-end close is run.

The 2027 social security wage base (192,300) is a typed constant with no source and could not be re-read; llms.txt links to the old github.io address; VENTURE.yaml still says stage: prototype; a binary ledger-1.0.1 wheel is checked into the venture directory; README.md is a 985-line mixed changelog and manual.

verdict: The accounting core is right and well tested. A hand-built month tied to the cent (profit 2,863.16, checking 7,475.16, card 112.00 with the card payment paired, not expensed), Schedule SE, the 2025 bracket schedule, a three-month Form 941/940 and standard loan payments all matched independent hand arithmetic, Pub. 946 Table A-1 and the 3-, 5- and 7-year mid-quarter columns matched the IRS PDF exactly, and a seeded period-end off-by-one in ledger.balances broke 12 of 2371 tests. It does not meet the bar because of claims and fitness, not arithmetic: llms.txt tells AI agents the product does not do payroll while it ships payroll worksheets, the headline 'second month' self-posting claim is 7% by the author's own benchmark, 96 MACRS cells for long-life property differ from the printed IRS tables by up to 0.05 points, and no reader has been shown on a real bank export, so a bookkeeper would use it as a reviewed first pass, not a book of record. Re-checkable: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture, and `node -e 'import("./taxforms.mjs").then(m=>console.log(m.selfEmployment(10000000,{year:2025}).tax/100))'` gives 14129.55.
